title: 2005 AMC10A 13
statement:
How many positive integers \(n\) satisfy the following condition:

\[ (130n)^{50} \gt n^{100} \gt 2^{200}? \]

solutions.text:
Taking \(50\)th roots, the condition becomes \(130n \gt n^2 \gt 2^4 = 16.\) From \(n^2 \gt 16\) we get \(n \gt 4,\) and from \(130n \gt n^2\) we get \(n \lt 130.\) So \(n\) ranges over the integers \(5, 6, \ldots, 129,\) which is \(125\) values.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: All quantities are positive, so take the \(50\)th root of each part of the inequality
The conditions become \(130n \gt n^2\) and \(n^2 \gt 16,\) which together give \(4 \lt n \lt 130\)
